guarantees.claim: b1 is always driven to b[3:2], b0 to b[1:0]; q1 to q[3:2], q0 to q[1:0]; t1 to t[3:2], t0 to t[1:0].

assumptions.claim: Inputs b, q, t are at least 4-bit vectors so that bit slices b[3:2], b[1:0], etc. are valid.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-range bit selects cause X propagation and can corrupt masked GF(2^4) values, potentially breaking the masking scheme.

uncertain_points.claim: Comment at lines 54-60 specifies a strict execution order for intermediate masking operations using b1,b0,q1,q0; however, this chunk only performs slicing. The actual GF operations in downstream logic must respect the order to avoid unmasked intermediate values. Without visibility, it's uncertain whether the order is enforced by combinational structure or sequential constraints.
uncertain_points.cond: When downstream logic computes c using these sliced signals
uncertain_points.risk: If the order is not enforced, transient unmasked values could appear, causing side-channel leakage and breaking masked AES security.
